newsitem.title: UK: UK rail body opens bids for 3 more rail franchises.
newsitem.headline: UK rail body opens bids for 3 more rail franchises.

text.p: The Office of Passenger rail Franchising (Opraf), the UK regulator in charge of selling off passenger services under the rail sell-off, opened the bidding for three more franchises on Monday.
Roger Salmon, franchising director, issued indicative bid invitations for Regional Railways North East, North West Regional Railways and Central Trains.
The deadline for indicative bids is 1400 GMT on October 24 for RRNE, October 28 for Central and October 30 for NWRR.
RRNE operates rail services in northern England, extending as far as the Scottish border and linking the east and west coasts of England, serving Manchester, Liverpool and Blackpool among others.
Its passenger revenue for the year ended March 31 1996 was 68 million stg. The company employs 2,981 million staff.
NWRR operates passenger services in north western England and north Wales. Its passenger revenue in the year ended March 31 1995 was 44 million stg. It has a staff of 2,910.
Central Trains covers central England and extends into Wales and East Anglia.
Revenue in the year ended March 31, 1995 was 60 million stg. It employs 2,639 people.
